I'm 69 years old and I've been farming these 2 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. My wife and I manage the land while our children work in the city factory. With only two of us and our age, we keep things simple and stick to what works. The soil here is good loam, and we have a well for irrigation when the rains don't come, but pumping costs money and labor so I don't waste water.

For winter wheat, I'll plant the improved variety we've used for years across the full 2.0 mu. I know this seed, and the seed shop in town gives me a fair price. I'll spread about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium. The fertilizer shop has good prices if I buy early. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings establish, once at jointing when the wheat really needs it, and once during grain filling. Too much water wastes electricity and can cause lodging. I'll use the rotary tiller after the maize comes off to prepare a good seedbed — the old way with animal ploughing is too hard on my back now. Two sprays for pests and weeds should be enough. I expect about 450 kg per mu if the spring frost stays away.

For summer maize, I'll plant hybrid seed right after the wheat harvest in early June — no time to waste, every day counts for the growing season. Same 2.0 mu. I'll use about 14 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat here; I'll irrigate twice if the summer is dry, especially at the big trumpet stage. Two pesticide applications depending on what I see in the field. Rotary till after wheat harvest to get the stubble broken up, then plant quickly. I should get around 500 kg per mu if the summer storms don't flatten it.

I don't chase the highest yields anymore — at my age, stable output with less labor and lower cost is better than gambling on new methods I don't fully trust. This plan has fed my family for decades and it will do fine this year.
